component.name: FaderFrame
component.summary: Record, edit, mix and master multitrack audio and MIDI

description.p: FaderFrame is a digital audio workstation for recording, editing, mixing and mastering. It routes audio through a realtime graph with buses, aux sends, sidechains, groups and VCAs, processes it on all cores with automatic plugin delay compensation, and hosts CLAP and VST3 plugins.

ul.li: Arranger with Pro Tools style edit modes, take comping, warping and fades
Analogue console style mixer with inserts, sends and metering
Piano roll, MIDI recording, MPE, MIDI clock and MTC sync
Automation with Touch, Latch and Write modes
Mastering tools: EBU R128 loudness, true peak, phase and spectrum
Native PipeWire and JACK on Linux
Skins from dark studio consoles to a light theme

screenshot.caption: The demo session playing in the Mixing workspace
The piano roll editing a MIDI clip
Mastering with loudness, level, phase and spectrum tools

description.p: Composition tools, project organisation and modulation.

ul.li: A key and a chord track that the piano roll and MIDI effects follow; arpeggiator, chord, scale and note echo before the instrument; MIDI Tools that transform and generate notes.
MIDI tracks with mixer strips that play instrument tracks, and Capture MIDI to turn what was played live into clips afterwards.
Folder tracks, clip aliases, project versions to compare and restore, a command palette with a shortcut editor and an undo history panel.
Modulators on any parameter: LFOs, envelope followers, step sequences, random, macros and per-note sources, with CLAP's non-destructive and polyphonic modulation.
Containers with parallel chains of devices, mixed and latency-aligned.
Samplers keep a sample's length when they change its pitch, take start and end points, and are made from audio selections.
A vinyl premaster for the album, with sides, checks and a cutting sheet.
A demo session that shows the new features.

description.p: Circuit-modelled microphone preamps in dedicated mixer input sections.

ul.li: Six preamp models with metallic faceplates, Gain and Master controls, automation and project recall.
Reusable GainStageFx circuit solver with worker processing, a 128-sample buffer and latency compensation.
Process instrument audio after the synth and preserve timing through freezing and bouncing.
Correct Tube 610 level control behaviour near zero gain.

description.p: Mixer editing, analogue crosstalk and reliable transport shortcuts.

ul.li: Reorder mixer tracks by dragging their name labels and resize loops by dragging either edge.
Newly chosen instruments appear in the visible plugin insert chain.
Show both EQ meter bars on mono tracks.
Optional project-wide analogue crosstalk between neighbouring mixer channels.
Space controls playback and stops recording before focused GTK buttons can consume it, while preserving text input.
Factory presets for built-in plugins, with undo and wet-only delay and reverb presets on effect returns.
Fix periodic GUI freezes during playback with the mixer and built-in plugin editors open.

The FaderFrame EQ: 24 bands with analogue-shaped curves to Nyquist, zero latency, natural or linear phase, dynamic and spectral bands keyed by their region or a sidechain, EQ Match, EQ Sketch, Spectrum Grab and an instance list.
The Program EQ: a circuit-modelled passive tube program equaliser with its own panel.
Dynamics: a compressor in five styles with a filtered sidechain, a true-peak lookahead limiter, a gate, expander and ducker, and a de-esser.

Effects: an oversampled saturator, a utility with vectorscope, a tempo-synced delay with tape and analogue styles, an algorithmic reverb in five types, chorus, ensemble, flanger, phaser and vibrato, and a tuner.

Instruments: a virtual analogue synth with unison, two envelopes and an LFO, a sampler that plays a sample across the keys or an SFZ instrument, and a sixteen-pad drum sampler; their samples are copied into the project.
Every device has an editor of its own with automation and MIDI learn from its controls.
Mastering meters: crest factor and the DR value next to the loudness range and PLR.
Sandboxed plugins: each CLAP, VST3 or Audio Unit instance can run in a process of its own on Linux, Windows and macOS; a crash no longer takes FaderFrame down.
VST3 program lists, 64-bit plugin processing, SysEx to plugins, native per-note expression for CLAP and VST3.
Render-ahead: tracks nobody plays live are processed ahead of the playhead on threads of their own; DSP workers at realtime priority everywhere and in the audio device's workgroup on macOS.

Mastering: loudness normalisation, true-peak limiting and noise-shaped dither on export; the album with per-song or album levelling, crossfades, a song's own inserts, ISRC/UPC and credits, a cue sheet and a verified DDP 2.00 CD master with CD-Text.
Editing: Quantize and Humanize for audio and MIDI, moving and copying song sections with their content, an Automation tab.
Portable mode on every platform and a portable Linux tarball.
